title: Causal Disentangled Anchor Learning for Scalable Fair Multi-view Clustering
claim: Prior methods inherit a spurious correlation between meaningful and protected factors; ours severs it via independence and orthogonality constraints in separate subspaces.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, causal graphs with a red crossed-out dashed link
description: Two side-by-side causal diagrams that use matching blue and red node colors. Panel (a), 'Biased data generation process', has a blue circle for semantic factors C and a red circle for sensitive factors S. A red dashed double-headed arc labeled 'Spurious Correlation' joins them. Solid arrows run from both circles down to a gray circle for observed data X. Panel (b), 'Causal disentanglement via CDAL', keeps C and S at the top. Each feeds a rounded box below it: blue Zu (Semantic Rep.) and red Zs (Sensitive Rep.). A red dashed arrow from S to Zu is crossed out with a red X and labeled 'HSIC Independence'. A gray dashed double arrow between the boxes is labeled 'Orthogonality'. Both boxes point to a gray circle for reconstructed data. The eye goes first to the crossed-out red arrow and the colored nodes.
caption: Illustration of the causal disentanglement mechanism versus the entangled data generation process. (a) The observed data X is generated by latent semantic factors C and sensitive factors S. A spurious correlation often exists between C and S due to historical biases. Traditional methods exploit this correlation, leading to biased outcomes. (b) Our framework simulates an intervention via structural constraints. It explicitly learns disentangled representations, Zu (semantic) and Zs (sensitive). The core mechanism severs the causal link between the sensitive factors S and the semantic representation Zu with the HSIC independence constraint, while orthogonality ensures subspace separation.
abstract: Existing fair multi-view clustering methods typically suffer from a severe trade-off between clustering utility and fairness, while incurring prohibitive quadratic complexity on large-scale datasets. To address these challenges, we propose Causal Disentangled Anchor Learning (CDAL), a novel framework that achieves scalable fairness via structural disentanglement. Guided by a structural causal model perspective, CDAL utilizes a dual-anchor mechanism to structurally separate latent representations into orthogonal semantic and sensitive subspaces. We further ensure statistical independence through a linearized Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) constraint, which is optimized via an efficient alternating scheme. Theoretically, we prove the identifiability of the disentangled factors and guarantee the algorithm's global convergence and linear time complexity $\mathcal{O}(n)$. Extensive experiments on large-scale benchmarks demonstrate that CDAL outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a superior utility-fairness trade-off. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Tracesource/CDAL.
